The promoted clauses faithfully incorporate the agreed clarification without new semantic choices and match the read-only reference implementation in crates/mori-core/src/ir.rs and crates/mori-core/src/runtime.rs: Transfer, Fee, and Liability resolve statement asset alias to declared AssetId A, whereas Discharge (whose Statement variant carries only name and amount ExprId) uses the existing duty row's AssetId, debtor, and creditor in S[i-1] when emitting its Liability effect; outer Step.value is the evaluated UInt amount q (including zero) as a typed Value::UInt object while statement.amount remains the zero-based ExprId; Step.snapshot retains complete canonically ordered state, balances, and liabilities (distinguishing absent from present-zero duties); and Step.effects / Execution.effects record single-statement deltas and their ordered concatenation.

All mandatory boundaries and open obligations are explicitly preserved in both documents: Mint, Burn, and dedicated accrual remain absent from Core/1 (and Liability amount addition is explicitly distinguished from interest/time-basis/day-count/accrual semantics); author/reviewer source exposure is disclosed; full independent financial expectations and runtime/consumer-byte conformance checks remain pending; all U0-U7, M1-M17, MC/SP/G, ACTUS/DeFi, composition, and target/proof/ledger exits remain open; and security/soundness/conservation/authorization remain with the designated security owner without gating permissionless developer use.

Author and reviewers were exposed to implementation source (crates/mori-core/src/ir.rs and crates/mori-core/src/runtime.rs); this review does not establish independent behavioral proof or test goldens.
Core/1 still lacks Mint, Burn, and dedicated accrual constructs, and explicit Liability amount addition does not satisfy interest, day-count, compounding, or accrual schedule obligations.
